content.title: About
content.content: A turkey sandwich with cheese is a sandwich or sub made with thinly sliced turkey breast, melted cheese, fresh vegetables and sauce, served on a soft roll. It is commonly offered in fast‑food restaurants and cafés.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turkey is a lean source of protein popular in the US and Europe.
Sub‑style sandwiches got their name from “submarine” because the roll resembles a submarine hull.
Cheese is often chosen to melt well, such as processed cheese, cheddar or mozzarella.
Some restaurants add cranberry sauce to turkey for a sweet‑savory contrast.
Turkey sandwiches are frequently served with fries or a side salad.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Turkey provides complete protein that supports muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Turkey breast contains less saturated fat than many other meats.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheese adds calcium, essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Turkey and cheese supply B6 and B12 vitamins, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Fiber from vegetables
items.content: Added lettuce, tomato, cucumber, etc., increase dietary fiber, aiding digestion.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese can trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Processed meats and sauces often contain high salt levels; those with hypertension should watch portions.

items.title: Proper cooking of turkey
items.content: Undercooked turkey may harbor harmful bacteria; cook to an internal temperature of 165 °F (74 °C).

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: A cheese‑laden sandwich can be calorie‑rich; portion control is advisable for weight management.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is typically eaten by hand, often cut in half. It pairs well with fries, a side salad, or a beverage. For a lighter option, choose a whole‑grain roll and reduced‑fat cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best enjoyed fresh. If you need to store it, wrap tightly in plastic film and keep refrigerated for up to 24 hours. Store turkey and cheese separately in airtight containers.
